name: Andrewes House
story: Vicar of St Giles Cripplegate from 1589 (arranged by Walsingham); said to speak fifteen languages.
completed_note: July or November 1969 depending on source; Phase III, John Laing; known as Block VIII until completed.
floors_note: Seven storeys above podium plus two below; top floor penthouses with barrel-vaulted roofs.
types: 13 flat types, 2- to 4-room; regular flats, penthouses, and two storeys of garden (sub-podium) flats. Only block whose garden flats have individual gardens/patios (facing Fore Street, behind a high wall).
views: Front-to-back (east-west) block along the south side of the lake. Living rooms face south over Fore Street; bedrooms face north over the lake. Sits between Gilbert House and Willoughby House.
nearest_station_entrance: Entrances on Andrewes Highwalk at podium level; street access from Fore Street and Wood Street via lift/stair 49 (next to the bar/restaurant). Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Penthouses with barrel-vaulted roofs; sub-podium garden flats with private gardens; tenants stores and car park at 03 level.
house_group: Andrewes House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Ben Jonson House
story: Taken out of school to lay bricks like his stepfather, he joined the army in Flanders and killed a Spanish soldier in single combat before taking up the theatre.
completed_note: March 1973; Phase IV, Myton (Taylor Woodrow).
floors_note: Seven residential floors above podium; no flats below podium. 52-bay block (list description).
types: Mostly maisonettes with internal stairs (corridors on levels 2, 3 and 5 only), plus two- and three-storey penthouses.
views: Longest terrace block in the estate, north podium, spans Golden Lane. North side looks over the Golden Lane Estate and a school playground; south side faces Frobisher Crescent, Defoe House and the Barbican Centre.
nearest_station_entrance: Lift 62 (west end) to Bridgewater Street; lift 63 (centre) to Beech Street; lift 64 (east end) to Whitecross Street. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Longest block; passes over Golden Lane; paired balconies on levels 2, 3 and 5; dolphin fountain at the front on Ben Jonson Place; round-arched glazed roof-level rooms.
house_group: Ben Jonson House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

photo_note: No file title names this block; taken from its Commons category, subject not verified.

name: Breton House
story: Son of a rich merchant of Red Cross Street (now buried under the estate); his stepfather was the poet George Gascoigne.
completed_note: November 1972; Phase IV, Myton (Taylor Woodrow).
floors_note: Seven storeys and rooftop (list description); 6 storeys of studios plus penthouse maisonettes.
types: Studios (types F1A, F2A) and one-bedroom penthouse maisonettes (type P2A).
views: North boundary of the estate, at right angles to the middle of Ben Jonson House. East flats overlook Whitecross Street; west flats overlook Cripplegate Library and Golden Lane. Mirror image of John Trundle Court.
nearest_station_entrance: Raised entrances up external stairs to lobbies serving clusters of five flats; lifts 65-67; fire exit to Golden Lane. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Rooftop penthouses with round-arched glazed form; raised mezzanine entrances; sub-podium level has no flats.
house_group: Breton House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Bryer Court
named_after: W. Bryer & Sons, gold refiners and assayers, who occupied 53-54 Barbican on the site
story: A frieze of the gold-refining process saved from their building is on the wall in White Lyon Court, facing Blake Tower.
completed_note: February 1973; Phase IV, Myton (Taylor Woodrow).
floors_note: Seven storeys above podium.
types: All studio flats (virtually identical); narrowest block on the estate.
views: North-south block on the north podium; all flats face west, single aspect (Murray House built 1956 stands directly behind). Its own small lake with fountains in Beech Gardens at the front.
nearest_station_entrance: Single entrance at the south (Ben Jonson House) end, via Fann Street ramp to north podium. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Narrowest block; small pool with fountains; access gallery at the rear.
house_group: Bryer Court (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

photo_note: No file title names this block; taken from its Commons category, subject not verified.

name: Bunyan Court
named_after: John Bunyan (1628-1688), writer and Baptist preacher
story: Son of a Bedford tinker who became a tinker himself; never went to school but learnt to read and write at home.
completed_note: December 1972; Phase IV, Myton (Taylor Woodrow).
floors_note: Seven storeys above podium (source page); list description says six storeys over an open ground floor.
flats_note: Derived from flat numbering 201-223, 301-323, 501-523 (3 x 23); source page gives no total.
types: Mainly two-storey maisonettes on a scissor plan around central corridors.
views: East-west block on the north podium forming the middle of a U with John Trundle Court and Bryer Court. North flats overlook Blake Tower; south flats overlook Beech Gardens.
nearest_station_entrance: Entrance and lift 59 at the Bryer Court end; built over the ramp from Fann Street. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Maisonettes with paired balconies on levels 2, 3 and 5; fitness centre beneath the podium; circular fountain pool.
house_group: Bunyan Court (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Cromwell Tower
story: Married Elizabeth Bourchier at St Giles Cripplegate in 1620 - the only link between Cromwell and the Barbican.
completed_note: January 1973; Phase III, John Laing.
floors_note: 43 storeys per Barbican Living and the list entry (garage, street foyer, 38 flat floors, 2 penthouse floors). CTBUH lists 42 floors.
flats_note: 108 flats + 3 penthouse maisonettes; three flats per floor.
types: Three large flats per floor, living rooms in the corners; penthouses of up to three storeys with roof gardens.
views: Triangular tower at Beech Street and Silk Street. Flat 1s: east rooms, north balconies; 2s: north-east rooms, west balconies; 3s: west rooms, south balconies. Eastern-most tower.
nearest_station_entrance: Main entrance at street level via Cromwell Place (Beech Street/Silk Street); podium entrance off Cromwell Highwalk. The tower is nearest to Moorgate. Station name for the entrance not stated.
features: Upswept cantilevered balconies on every floor; jagged stepped top with penthouses and roof gardens; staffed foyer; 3 high-speed lifts; dramatic first-floor podium foyer. 123 m is the CTBUH architectural height.
house_group: Cromwell Tower (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

photos.author: Tom Parnell from Scottish Borders, Scotland

name: Defoe House
named_after: Daniel Defoe (1660-1731), novelist, spy and journalist
story: Born Daniel Foe in the parish of St Giles Cripplegate; added the "De" himself. The block is pronounced De-FOE.
completed_note: December 1973; Phase II, Turriff then John Laing after disputes (known as Block IV).
floors_note: Seven storeys above podium plus two beneath; 12 bays.
types: Regular flats, 24 rooftop penthouses with barrel-vaulted roofs, and sub-podium garden flats (view over Thomas More Garden, no direct access).
views: Front-to-back block on the north side of Thomas More Garden. Living rooms face south over the garden/lake; bedrooms face north over Beech Gardens, Shakespeare Tower and Defoe Place.
nearest_station_entrance: Glazed entrances on Defoe Place at podium level for each of 12 staircases; staircase 1 opens at street level onto Lauderdale Place. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Penthouses; garden flats; tenants stores; Defoe House/Shakespeare Tower car park (entrance off Beech Street).
house_group: Defoe House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Frobisher Crescent
named_after: Sir Martin Frobisher, Elizabethan seaman and privateer
story: Chosen to test Humphrey Gilbert's theory of a north-west passage; also held a privateering licence from Elizabeth I.
completed_note: Probably 1982 with the Barbican Centre (Barbican Living: no precise date); flats converted 2008-2010 (United House), 69 flats on levels 7-9.
floors_note: Nine levels: 1-3 car parking/void, 4-6 Barbican Centre, 7-9 flats.
types: Studios, 1, 2 and 3-bed apartments; top-floor flats have barrel-arched roofs with mezzanines; all have balconies, end flats wrap-around terraces.
views: Crescent north-west of the Barbican Centre, between Shakespeare Tower and the Centre; based on the old Jewin Crescent; straddles the north and south podia. Looks onto the "sculpture court" inside the crescent.
nearest_station_entrance: Part of the Barbican Centre complex; link to the Centre on the east side. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Designed as flats but turned into offices in the 1970s; fittings put in storage. Used by City University Business School, then converted: United House / TP Bennett, JCT D&B contract GBP 13.5m, Aug 2008-Jun 2010, flats sold by the City.
house_group: Frobisher Crescent (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Gilbert House
story: Lived in Redcross Street, whose route runs exactly under Gilbert House; Raleigh's half-brother and champion of the north-west passage.
completed_note: August 1969; Phase III, John Laing.
floors_note: 5 storeys of flats + 2 of penthouses, all above podium; stands on stilts in the lake.
types: 1- to 5-room flats and penthouses; side-to-side with central corridor; no garden flats.
views: Straddles the lake on tall stilts; Gilbert Bridge runs underneath. West flats look over the Barbican Centre terrace and lake; east flats look over the waterfall, towards Willoughby House.
nearest_station_entrance: Main entrance at podium level on Gilbert Bridge; lifts 50A/50B (south, near The Postern) and 52 (north). Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Built on stilts over the lake; pub (Crowders) under the south end of the bridge; foundation stone of the Arts Centre at the north end.
house_group: Gilbert House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: John Trundle Court
story: Published the "bad quarto" pirate Hamlet in 1603 with Nicholas Ling.
completed_note: October 1972; Phase IV, Myton (Taylor Woodrow).
floors_note: Eight storeys including mezzanine entrance level (source page); list description says seven plus mezzanine.
types: Studios (types F1A and F2A) and one-bedroom duplex penthouses (type P2A).
views: North-south block on the western edge of the estate along Aldersgate Street. West flats overlook Aldersgate Street and Barbican Tube station; east flats overlook Beech Gardens. Mirror image of Breton House.
nearest_station_entrance: Via Fann Street ramp to the north podium or Beech Gardens/John Trundle Highwalk; lifts 55-58; lift 55 reaches Aldersgate Street near the bridge to Barbican Tube. Overlooks Barbican station.
features: Mezzanine entrances up tiled steps; rooftop glazed penthouses; Virgin Active gym partly under the block.
house_group: John Trundle Court (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

photo_note: No file title names this block; taken from its Commons category, subject not verified.

name: Lambert Jones Mews
named_after: Richard Lambert Jones (1783-1863), Common Councilman for Cripplegate Without
story: His 1824 motion to the Court of Common Council led to the founding of the Guildhall Library.
completed_note: February 1974; Phase II, Turriff then John Laing.
floors_note: Two-storey houses with roof gardens.
flats_note: Eight houses (Estate Office classes them as flats).
types: Two-storey mews houses, each with a garage; roof gardens.
views: East-facing onto Thomas More Garden (many have back doors straight onto the garden); front doors onto a cobbled mews road below Lauderdale Place.
nearest_station_entrance: Front doors on the cobbled mews road below Lauderdale Place, entrance shared with Thomas More Car Park off Aldersgate Street. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Only homes with back doors straight onto a garden; roof gardens; garages.
house_group: Lambert Jones Mews (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

photo_note: No file title names this block; taken from its Commons category, subject not verified.

name: Lauderdale Tower
story: Built on the site of the London house of the Scottish earls of Lauderdale; first earl John Maitland was created in 1624.
completed_note: October 1974; Phase II, Turriff then John Laing.
floors_note: 44 storeys (garage, street foyer, 40 flat floors, 2 penthouse floors). CTBUH lists 42.
types: Three large flats per floor in the corners; penthouse maisonettes.
views: Western-most tower, close to Barbican Tube and Aldersgate Street; overlooks Thomas More Garden. Flat 1s: west rooms/north balconies; 2s: north rooms/east balconies; 3s: east rooms/south balconies.
nearest_station_entrance: Main entrance at street level via Lauderdale Place off Beech Street; podium entrance off the highwalk. Close to Barbican Tube station.
features: Upswept balconies; jagged penthouse tops with roof gardens; 3 high-speed lifts; staffed foyer. Featured in TV drama Luther.
house_group: Lauderdale Tower (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Mountjoy House
story: Shakespeare lodged with the Mountjoy family (Barbican Living: Monkwell Street, 1598-1612; City of London: Silver Street, 1604 - sources differ).
completed_note: April 1971; Phase II, Turriff then John Laing.
floors_note: 5 storeys of flats with penthouse maisonettes above.
types: 2- to 5-room flats and penthouses, mostly identical to Gilbert House; side-to-side, central corridor, no garden flats.
views: North-south block joined to Thomas More House ("zig" to Seddon's "zag"), on tall columns above Mountjoy Close. East flats overlook St Giles Terrace, the small lake, the City Wall and Bastion; west flats overlook the City of London School for Girls grounds.
nearest_station_entrance: Lifts/stairs 25 (north, near Thomas More House) and 26 (south, shared with a public route). Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Unusually tall columns; ceremonial stairs to the lakeside (cut off); rooftop penthouses.
house_group: Mountjoy House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

photo_note: No file title names this block; taken from its Commons category, subject not verified.

name: Seddon House
story: Converted London House, Aldersgate Street, into England's first big furniture store.
completed_note: May 1974; Phase II, Turriff then John Laing.
floors_note: 6 storeys of flats above podium plus penthouse maisonettes (list description: seven storeys).
types: Studios to five-room penthouse maisonettes; side-to-side with central corridor.
views: Runs from Lauderdale Tower to Thomas More House on the west side of Thomas More Garden; rooms face west over the garden or east over Aldersgate Street.
nearest_station_entrance: Entrances at both ends; main entrance at podium level on Seddon Highwalk; 01 level is Lauderdale Place. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Tall columns; rooftop penthouses (two bays wide); granite-faced lift lobbies at the north end.
house_group: Seddon House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

photos.author: Tom Parnell from Scottish Borders, Scotland

photo_note: No file title names this block; taken from its Commons category, subject not verified.

name: Shakespeare Tower
story: Lodged with the Mountjoy family near the Barbican; the tower was long cited as Europe's highest residential building.
completed_note: February 1976; Phase Va, Sir Robert McAlpine - last building completed.
floors_note: 44 storeys (garage, street foyer, 40 flat floors, 2 penthouse floors). CTBUH lists 42.
types: Three large flats per floor; penthouse maisonettes.
views: Centre tower, just west of the Barbican Centre; stands in the south podium, linked to the north podium. Flat 1s: south rooms/east balconies; 2s: east rooms/north balconies; 3s: north rooms/west balconies.
nearest_station_entrance: Main entrance from Defoe Place at south podium level; second entrance off Beech Garden on the north podium. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Upswept balconies; penthouses with roof gardens; Guinness Book of Records highest residential building in Europe for many years.
house_group: Shakespeare Tower (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Speed House
story: Probably born in St Paul's churchyard; freed from the family tailoring trade by Sir Fulk Greville's patronage to pursue maps.
completed_note: July 1969; first Barbican block built; Phase III, John Laing (Block VI).
floors_note: Seven storeys above podium with two below; eight bays.
flats_note: Flats, maisonettes and penthouses; 2 to 5 rooms.
types: Regular flats; penthouses; two-storey garden maisonettes below podium (mainly Type 84).
views: Front-to-back block in the north-east corner; forms the northern edge of Speed Gardens; living rooms look south over the garden and lake (sub-podium flats south only).
nearest_station_entrance: Doors at podium level on Speed Highwalk; street-level access from Silk Street beside the Guildhall School. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Garden maisonettes with car ports; penthouses with barrel vaults; Speed Garden playground.
house_group: Speed House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Thomas More House
named_after: Sir Thomas More (1478-1535), lawyer, statesman and saint
story: Born in Milk Street; "the King's good servant, but God's first".
completed_note: September 1973; Phase II, Turriff then John Laing (Block XI).
floors_note: Six floors of flats plus one of penthouses above podium; three storeys of garden flats below.
types: Regular flats; penthouses; three storeys of garden flats below podium (lowest studios, two upper levels larger).
views: Front-to-back block along Thomas More Garden, the largest of the Barbican gardens. Above-podium living rooms face south over the City of London School for Girls tennis courts; north view over the garden. Garden flats face the garden.
nearest_station_entrance: Glazed doors at podium level on Thomas More Highwalk; gates onto Thomas More Garden; 03-level entrance on the cobbled road to the car park. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Garden flats facing the largest garden; penthouses; Thomas More Car Park at 03 level.
house_group: Thomas More House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Willoughby House
story: Married Charles Brandon, owner of the Barbican manor, in 1533; the name revives the old Willoughby House that stood here.
completed_note: April 1971; Phase III, John Laing.
floors_note: Six floors of flats with penthouse maisonettes above (list description: seven storeys).
types: Mostly "up and over" scissor maisonettes plus penthouse maisonettes; flats are rarely identical.
views: Eastern edge of the estate, runs from Speed House to Andrewes House. Living rooms face west over the lake (past Brandon Mews domes); bedrooms face east over Moor Lane / Britannic Tower.
nearest_station_entrance: Main entrances on Willoughby Highwalk; lifts at both ends and centre. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Up-and-over maisonettes; the estate's eastern edge; planted Willoughby Highwalk.
house_group: Willoughby House (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Brandon Mews
named_after: The Brandon family, lords of the manor of Barbican
story: Charles Brandon, Duke of Suffolk, held the manor of Base Court (Barbican); earlier Robert Brandon (d.1369), son of Lord Ufford, acquired it.
completed_note: November 1969; Phase III, John Laing.
floors_note: Two-storey houses below podium level.
flats_note: 26 houses (Estate Office classes them as flats).
types: Two-storey mews houses with internal bathrooms and angled roof lights; brown perspex roof canopy added in the 1980s.
views: West-facing; views over the lake behind the waterfall or over Speed Garden (no direct access).
nearest_station_entrance: Entrances down from podium on Willoughby Highwalk, each serving two houses; parking by the rear doors. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Roof canopy of brown perspex (1980s); water chute / waterfall into the lake.
house_group: Brandon Mews (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: The Postern
named_after: The postern: a back door or side gate, here referring to the posterns in the City Wall at Cripplegate
story: Barbican Living defines a postern via the OED as a back door or side gate, in the context of the City Wall gates of Cripplegate ward.
completed_note: March 1971; Phase II, Turriff then John Laing.
floors_note: Four-storey houses over a basement.
flats_note: 7 town houses, a maisonette, a flat and the Rectory of St Giles'; numbered 1-10.
types: Long narrow town houses with garages, open-tread dog-leg stairs, roof gardens.
views: Overlook St Giles Church and the lake extension between the church and the City Wall.
nearest_station_entrance: Front doors on the covered Postern Bridge towards London Wall; stairs down to St Giles Terrace. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Glazed engineering brick cladding; link between Gilbert Bridge and Wallside.
house_group: No formal House Group (Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Wallside
named_after: The Roman / City Wall beside it
story: Runs parallel to surviving remains of the Roman wall.
completed_note: March 1971; Phase II, Turriff then John Laing.
floors_note: Four storeys, set on, above and below podium.
flats_note: Sixteen town houses (incl. a doctor's surgery with flat and a dentist's surgery).
types: Town houses with integral garages and roof terraces; entered at podium level.
views: The only part of the estate where homes face outward; front overlooks Bridgewater Square, back overlooks St Giles Terrace, the lake and the City Wall.
nearest_station_entrance: Street doors on the square; upper entrances from the highwalk. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Roof terraces; Roman wall views; glazed engineering brick.
house_group: Wallside (house group per Barbican Association who's who)

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Milton Court / The Heron
story: Replaced the demolished Milton Court (a fire station, medical facilities and flats). Not part of the Grade II listing.
completed_note: Completed September 2013 per Wikipedia / CTBUH.
floors_note: 36 storeys (Wikipedia / CTBUH).
types: Studios, apartments, panoramics and penthouses.
views: Corner of Silk Street and Moor Lane, next to the Guildhall School.
nearest_station_entrance: Close to Barbican and Moorgate Tube stations (Wikipedia).
features: Guildhall School annexe in the lower six floors; eight-storey atrium.
house_group: heronleaseholders.com (Wikipedia infobox website; not checked)

name: Blake Tower (former YMCA)
category: adjacent - not part of the estate proper
story: Named for the poet and painter; no namesake story on the sources fetched.
completed_note: Built 1965-71 as the Barbican YMCA (Phase IV, Myton); converted 2015-16 by Redrow Homes for the City. Note: brief said 2017 - sources found say 2015-16.
floors_note: HE list: 16-storey tower. Barbican Living: two lower-ground floors, ground, floors 1-15, duplexes on 16-17.
types: Studios to 3-bed; mostly 1- and 2-bed; two duplexes on floors 16-17.
views: On Fann Street beside the ramp from Goswell Road; links the Barbican to the Golden Lane Estate (height echoes Great Arthur House).
nearest_station_entrance: 2 Fann Street, EC2Y 8BR, by the Goswell Road ramp. Nearest Tube not stated on source.
features: Exotic projecting concrete fire-escape stairs; design echoes Golden Lane tower height. Barbican Living treats it as an estate block; it is owned by the City and covered by the same 2001 list entry (as "YMCA"), though physically separate.
house_group: Blake Tower (house group per Barbican Association who's who); named in the 2020 BA newsletter, absent from the current who's who table

listing_entry.note: Single list entry for the whole Barbican complex (listed 5 Sep 2001); blocks are not separately listed.

name: Golden Lane Estate
story: Chamberlin, Powell and Bon's first big commission, won in the 1951-52 competition; built 1953-62 for City workers as council housing; the Barbican followed on the south side.
floors_note: Great Arthur House: 16 storeys (LGC; HE-derived text says 17 including ground-floor offices).
flats_note: Total not found; block counts in LGC piece: Great Arthur House 120, Cullum Welch 72, Basterfield 54, etc.
features: Great Arthur House was briefly London's tallest residential building and the first to break the 100 ft limit; Crescent House Grade II*.

listing_entry.note: Great Arthur House only (estate listed 1997; Crescent House II*; other blocks have separate entries not retrieved).
